result_text:
I fixed the four default scoping conventions in `ScopingConventions.java`, and they now match the files they were meant for. The full `codeanalyzer` test suite passes (334 tests, 3 skipped), including a new test I added.

Changes, all in `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventions.java`:

- **Generated HTML pages:** the pkgdown, Doxygen and meta-generator rules had `(html|html|xhtml)`. They now read `(html|htm|xhtml)`, so `.htm` pages are covered and `.html`/`.xhtml` still match.
- **.NET documentation XML:** `.*/[.]xml` became `.*[.]xml`, so `MyAssembly.xml` matches. The `<doc>` check still only looks at the first 2 lines.
- **JavaScript generated by a tool:** `.*/[.]js` became `.*[.]js`, so `app.js` matches on its `// Generated by …` line.
- **Gradle JavaScript scripts:** `.*[.][-]gradle[.]js` became `.*[-]gradle[.]js`, so `build-gradle.js` matches. `build.gradle` is still matched by its own rule.

I also added `codeanalyzer/src/test/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventionsTest.java`. It checks each of the four fixed cases, plus negative cases: a hand-written `.htm`/`.html` page, a `.js` file without the generated header, an `.xml` file with `<doc>` past line 2, and a plain `app.js` outside the build scope.

I did not run the new test against the original file to confirm it fails there; the failure is implied by the typos but not observed. Nothing is committed.
